why:
I checked every command in both briefs. Most of them would run as written: the files they name exist, `npm test` matches package.json (the issue's proof uses `npm run test:cli`, which doesn't exist), `cmp -` and `grep -n -- '--tsv'` take valid arguments, and the JS in the tests is valid.

Check 5 in the verifier brief breaks the criterion. Its main command `printf '[{"a\\\\tb":"1\\\\t2"}]\n' > /tmp/e5` is in single quotes, so printf sees `\\\\t`. printf turns each `\\` into one backslash, so the file gets `a\\tb` with two backslashes instead of the one-backslash JSON escape `a\tb`. The `cmp` would then report a difference on a correct PR, so the check fails falsely. The brief admits this with "adjust the escaping if needed" and offers a `node -e` fallback that does work. Still, the command as written gives the wrong expected bytes.
